quran.note: The messengers give Ibrahim’s wife news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya’qub; she wonders, “shall I give birth while I am an old woman?”
The guests of Ibrahim give him good news of a learned boy.
Good tidings of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous; Allah blessed him and Ibrahim.
Allah gave Ibrahim Ishaq and Ya’qub and made each a prophet.
Ishaq and Ya’qub made leaders guiding by Allah’s command.
Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya’qub, “those of strength and [religious] vision”, chosen for remembrance of the Hereafter.
Prophethood and Scripture placed in Ibrahim’s descendants.

hadith.summary: Asked who was the most honoured of people with Allah, the Prophet ﷺ said the most righteous. When they said that was not what they meant, he said Yusuf, a prophet of Allah, the son of a prophet, the son of a prophet, the son of the khalil of Allah. The report then turns to the Arabs and their understanding of the religion.
hadith.note: The report names no one but Yusuf; it is read as giving the line Yusuf, Ya’qub, Ishaq, Ibrahim, each described as a prophet. That reading is ours, from the order of the Qur’an (12:6; 2:133), not a statement in the report.

scholarly.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
scholarly.author: Ibn Kathir
scholarly.summary: Records the argument of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi that Ishaq could not be the son Ibrahim was told to sacrifice, because 11:71 gave his mother the news of Ishaq and, after him, Ya’qub, so a son of Ishaq was promised before he could be sacrificed. Ibn Kathir concludes the son was Ismail. This is the view of that work; see the disagreement below.

differences.question: Which son was Ibrahim told to sacrifice (37:102)?

views.who: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Mujahid, al-Sha’bi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Imam Ahmad and others listed by Ibn Kathir
views.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com), on 37:102
views.view: Ismail. Ibn Kathir holds this view and treats Ishaq as a mistaken identification.

views.who: The Jewish text, as Ibn Kathir describes it
views.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com), on 37:102; the Bible text (Genesis 22:1-14, NRSVUE) read on BibleGateway
views.view: The Bible names the son as Isaac (Genesis 22:2, read by us on BibleGateway). Ibn Kathir argues that the name was inserted into the Jewish text.

differences.note: The Qur’an does not name the son (37:99-107). The good news of Ishaq is given afterwards (37:112).
